blocks.text: Mr. Mark Green, Chief Financial Officer, Franklin-Snyder
Dear Mr. Green:

This letter confirms that this office will design the relocation of the utilities in conflict with your planned improvements, and it sets out the terms of that work. It covers the scope, the people who will do it, the fee, and the conditions under which we will proceed. When you have read it and returned a signed copy to this office, it will stand as our agreement to perform the work for {{fact:f:E-2006-001.client}}.
The Work to Be Performed

Your development cannot proceed until the utilities that cross the site are moved clear of the proposed building, grading, and pavement. We will design that relocation. Our work begins with the record drawings, the survey, and field locates that fix where the existing water main, sanitary sewer, and overhead electric and telephone lines actually lie. We will confirm each conflict against your site plan. We will then design a new alignment and profile for each utility that must move, clear of the improvements and clear of one another, and we will prepare the tie-in details where the relocated lines rejoin the existing system.

The design will meet the standard of each utility that owns the line. The water main is operated by the regional water authority, and we will design its relocation to that authority's specifications and carry the coordination with its staff. The electric and telephone relocations will be designed to the serving companies' requirements. We will prepare the relocation plan and profile sheets under a sealed cover sheet, the easement exhibits for the new alignments, the estimated quantities, and an opinion of probable construction cost. Our fee includes one round of revisions to answer the written comments of the reviewing parties.
Reliance on Furnished Information

Our design will rely on the record drawings, the survey, and the site plan furnished to us. We will check that information for consistency and confirm the critical utilities by field locate, but we are entitled to rely on what is furnished and are not responsible for errors it contains. If the site plan or the survey changes after we begin, the change may affect the design, the schedule, and the fee. We will tell you the effect before we act on it.
Who Will Do the Work

The work will be staffed from this office. Linda George, Project Engineer, will lead the design and carry the day-to-day coordination with the utility owners and with the regional water authority. Jason Jordan, Design Technician, will prepare the plan and profile sheets and the relocation details to her direction. Mark Todd, Principal Engineer, will review every sheet and seal the completed set, and correspondence to the regional water authority or to any other public body will be issued over his signature. Questions on the progress of the work should be directed to Linda George. Questions on scope, fee, or the terms of this agreement should be directed to Mark Todd.
Fee and Commencement

Our fee for the work described above is a fixed sum of {{fact:f:E-2006-001.fee}}. That sum covers the design, the plan and profile sheets, the easement exhibits, the quantities and cost opinion, and the single round of revisions noted above. We will begin the work on {{fact:f:E-2006-001.start}}. Work outside this scope, including further revision rounds, redesign to follow a change in your site plan, or the design of utilities not now in conflict, will be undertaken only on your written authorization, and we will quote its cost before we proceed.
Invoicing and Payment

We will invoice monthly for the work completed in the period. Each invoice is due within thirty days of its date. Reimbursable costs, such as reproduction, agency fees, and delivery, are billed at cost and are additional to the fee. If an invoice stands unpaid sixty days after its date, we may suspend the work until it is paid, and we will give written notice before we do. A suspension for non-payment extends our schedule by its length.
Duration and Termination

This agreement takes effect on the day the work begins and runs until the relocation plans are complete and the reviewing parties' first comments have been answered. Either of us may end it on ten days' written notice to the other. On termination by you, you will pay for the services performed and the costs incurred through the date of termination. The drawings, profiles, and calculations we prepare are our instruments of service and remain our property; on payment in full you may use them for this project.
Confidentiality

We will hold in confidence the site information, plans, and financial figures you give us, and we will use them only for this work. We may disclose what a utility owner or a public body reasonably requires for its review, and what the law compels. This obligation outlasts the completion or termination of the work.
Limit of Our Liability

We will perform this work with the care and skill ordinarily used by civil engineers practicing in this locality at this time. We make no other warranty, express or implied. Our total liability to {{fact:f:E-2006-001.client}} for any claim arising out of or related to this work, whether in contract or in tort, is limited to the amount of the fee paid under this agreement. We are not responsible for the means, methods, or safety of construction, nor for the acts of contractors or others not under our direct control.
Governing Law
This agreement is governed by the laws of the state in which the site lies. Any dispute under it that we cannot settle between us will be brought in the courts of that state.
Schedule

The work runs about three months from the start. We can hold that schedule so long as the record information reaches us when it is needed and the utility owners respond within their usual time. Delay in either is outside our control. Should one threaten the completion of the work, we will tell you promptly and propose how to recover the time.
Acceptance

If these terms are acceptable, please sign both copies of this letter and return one to this office. On receipt we will schedule the work to begin on the date stated above. If any term needs discussion, telephone before you sign and we will settle it first.
Sincerely,
To: The engagement team
From: Linda George, Project Engineer
Re: Kickoff, Utility Relocation Design for Franklin-Snyder

We have begun the utility relocation design for {{fact:f:E-2006-001.client}}, and our object is a single, buildable relocation design that clears the utility owners and the regional water authority on the first review, so that Franklin-Snyder can move the lines and open its site on the schedule it has set. Everything that follows serves that object, and I want us working from one picture of it before any sheet is drawn.

We have about three months, which is adequate for a relocation of this size only if we hold the sequence and avoid rework, because the surest way to lose the time is to design a line against a record we have not verified and then redraw it when the field proves the record wrong, and that is the one thing this memo is meant to keep us from doing.

The work started on {{fact:f:E-2006-001.start}}, and it divides into four workstreams that must proceed in order, since each rests on the one before it and a mistake carried forward is far more costly to correct than one caught at its source.

items: Existing utilities and conflicts. I will assemble the record drawings, the survey, and the field locates, and I will fix where the water main, the sanitary sewer, and the overhead lines actually lie before we design anything to move them.

Relocation design. From that base I will lay out a new alignment and profile for each line that must move, clear of the proposed improvements and clear of the other utilities, and I will set the tie-ins where each relocated line rejoins the system.

Owner and agency coordination. I will carry the coordination with the regional water authority for the water main and with the serving companies for the electric and telephone lines, so that each relocation is designed to the standard its owner will accept.

Sheets and drafting. Jason Jordan will prepare the plan and profile sheets, the relocation details, and the easement exhibits from my direction, and he will check every callout against the design memoranda so the set tells one consistent story.

blocks.text: The regional water authority owns the water main, and its relocation is the line that will most shape our schedule, because its review is the one we least control; for that reason I intend to open the conversation with the authority's staff while the alignment is still on paper and easy to change, instead of presenting them a finished design and hoping it passes. The serving electric and telephone companies will each hold us to their own standards, and I have asked for those standards so that we design to them from the start.
Where we begin

Our first effort goes to the existing utilities, and we will not lay out a single relocation until we agree that we know what is in the ground, because a relocation designed against a wrong record is worse than none at all. I will circulate the base once the locates are in, and we will confirm the conflicts together before Jason Jordan turns any sheet. Mark Green, the Chief Financial Officer at Franklin-Snyder, is the owner's contact for site access and for the developer's decisions, and I will route the owner's questions through him so that we speak to the client with one voice.

Bring me any assumption you have to make and I will see it filed, so that the next person designs from what we know and not from memory. Let us meet at the end of the week to walk the conflicts once the first locates are back.
Progress Meeting: Utility Relocation Design for Franklin-Snyder

These minutes record a working session held to review the relocation design at its midpoint, to reconcile the design against the field locates now returned, and to settle the open items with the owner. The design is progressing on the schedule set at the outset of the work, and no change to its scope was raised.
Attendees

items: Linda George, Project Engineer, Brackenridge Civil Group
Jason Jordan, Design Technician, Brackenridge Civil Group
Mark Green, Chief Financial Officer, Franklin-Snyder

blocks.text: Matters Discussed

Linda George presented the existing-conditions base as it now stands, reconciled against the field locates and the test pits taken since the last review. The locates confirmed the water main and the sanitary sewer substantially where the record drawings placed them, but the overhead electric was found to cross the parcel some distance off its recorded position, which narrows the corridor available for the relocated lines. It was agreed that the design would carry the located position rather than the record, and that the discrepancy would be noted on the plan for the serving utility's confirmation.

Jason Jordan reported that the plan and profile sheets are drawn to the preliminary alignment, and he identified a conflict between the proposed sanitary relocation and the new water main alignment at their crossing, where the vertical separation falls short of the regional water authority's required standard. It was agreed that Linda George would lower the sanitary profile at the crossing to restore the separation, and that Jason Jordan would revise the affected sheets once the corrected profile is set.

Linda George reported on the coordination with the regional water authority, whose staff have reviewed the preliminary water main alignment informally and have asked that the relocated main be carried outside the proposed building footprint by a stated margin and placed within a dedicated easement. The easement exhibits will be prepared to reflect that margin. No formal comments have yet issued, the review to date having been by conversation only.

Coordination with the serving electric and telephone companies was also discussed, the two lines being carried on the same poles and therefore to be relocated together. Linda George reported that the electric company has provided its relocation standard and its lead time for the work, and that the telephone company's requirements are expected shortly. It was agreed that the relocation of the joint-use poles would be shown on a separate sheet, so as to keep each utility owner's review confined to its own facilities.

Mark Green confirmed, on behalf of the owner, that the site plan is settled and that the building footprint shown to this office will not change, which allows the relocations to be fixed against a stable improvement. He further confirmed that the owner will secure the temporary construction access the utility contractor will require, and that the record drawings for the private service lines on the property would be furnished within the week.

The schedule for the relocation design for {{fact:f:E-2006-001.client}} was reviewed and found to be holding at its midpoint, with no additional work requested and no change to the agreed scope contemplated.
Action Items

rows: Lower the sanitary relocation profile at the water main crossing to restore the required separation
Revise the plan and profile sheets to the corrected profile and the located electric position
Prepare the easement exhibits to the margin set by the regional water authority
Furnish the record drawings for the private service lines

blocks.text: The next step is the correction of the sanitary profile at the crossing, on which the revised sheets depend; once it is set, Jason Jordan will turn the affected sheets and the team will meet again at the next scheduled progress review.
Status Report: Utility Relocation Design

The utility relocation design for {{fact:f:E-2006-001.client}} has reached its midpoint on schedule and within its budget, and nothing in the work to date suggests that either the schedule or the fixed fee is at risk. This report sets out where the design now stands, what was completed in the period, what the second half will hold, and the two items we are watching. None of it asks a decision of you today; it is a record of steady progress on the relocation Franklin-Snyder needs before its site work can begin.
Where the design stands

The design is roughly half complete. The existing utilities have been located in the field and reconciled against the record drawings, the conflicts with your proposed improvements have been confirmed, and a preliminary alignment and profile have been laid out for each line that must move. We have passed out of the investigation and into the design proper, where the alignments are refined, the crossings are resolved, and each relocation is carried to the standard its utility owner will accept.

The work is tracking with our costs, and we remain within the fixed fee of {{fact:f:E-2006-001.fee}} for the engagement, with nothing in the remaining work that we expect to change that. No additional scope has been requested, and the design has not grown beyond the relocation of the utilities identified at the outset as being in conflict with the improvements.
Completed in this period

The field locates and test pits were completed and the base reconciled against them. The water main and the sanitary sewer were found substantially where the record placed them, but the overhead electric was located some distance off its recorded position, and the design now carries the located position rather than the record, which is the more reliable of the two and keeps us from designing a relocation against a line that is not where the paper says it is.

Jason Jordan has drawn the plan and profile sheets to the preliminary alignment and, in doing so, found a conflict at the crossing of the relocated sanitary sewer and the relocated water main, where the vertical separation fell short of the regional water authority's standard. The sanitary profile is being lowered at that crossing to restore the separation, and the affected sheets will be revised to the corrected profile, so that the conflict is resolved on paper well before it could reach the field.

The coordination with the utility owners has begun in earnest. The regional water authority has reviewed the preliminary water main alignment informally and has asked that the relocated main be carried outside your building footprint by a stated margin and placed within a dedicated easement, and the easement exhibits are being prepared to that margin. The serving electric company has provided its relocation standard and its lead time, and the telephone company's requirements are expected shortly.
The second half

In the second half we will finish the alignments and profiles, resolve the remaining crossings, and complete the easement exhibits, the estimated quantities, and the opinion of probable construction cost. The relocation of the joint-use electric and telephone poles will be carried on its own sheet, so that each utility owner's review is confined to its own facilities and no owner is asked to pass on another's design.

Jason Jordan will turn the plan set from the completed design, and the set will be assembled under the sealed cover sheet for issue. We will bring the design to you for a review before it is finalized and before it is submitted to the utility owners for their formal approval, so that you see the relocation as it will be built and can raise anything that does not match the owner's intent while it is still easy to change.
Items we are watching

Two items bear watching, and neither is serious today. The first is the formal review by the regional water authority, which to this point has been by conversation only; until its written comments are in hand, the water main alignment carries the authority's informal guidance rather than its approval, and a formal comment could ask for a change we have not anticipated.

The second is the private service information for the site. Until the owner's record drawings for the private service lines are in hand, the design carries an assumption about those lines that we would prefer to confirm before the plan set is issued; the drawings were promised within the week, and once they are in, that assumption can be retired.
Where this leaves us

The relocation design is at its midpoint, on schedule, and within the fee, and the path to an issued plan set is clear. The open items are the ordinary ones of a relocation at this stage, and both are on their way to being closed. We will bring the design to you at the review before it is finalized.
Prepared by Linda George, Project Engineer.
